reason: The docs show training a model with run_local.sh on CIFAR-10 (public dataset, no keys), and the small LeNet variant can finish a short training run on CPU.
demo: Installation/Tutorial docs: ./scripts/run_local.sh nets/lenet_at_cifar10_run.py (full-precision learner on CIFAR-10, local mode)
goal: Get PocketFlow's local-mode training working on CPU: running nets/lenet_at_cifar10_run.py (as scripts/run_local.sh does, with path.conf pointing data_dir_local_cifar10 at the CIFAR-10 binary version) with --nb_epochs_rat 0.01 must train the LeNet full-precision learner and save a checkpoint to ./models_eval/model.ckpt. Then `--exec_mode eval` should evaluate the model on the CIFAR-10 test set. You will need a Python and TensorFlow 1.x-compatible environment (the code uses tf.app.flags, tf.layers). Download CIFAR-10 binary from https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~kriz/cifar-10-binary.tar.gz. Put the Python environment setup in /work/env.sh, and /work/run.sh is not needed.
check: The hidden test runs a short CPU training of the LeNet CIFAR-10 model through the repo's own entry script, then checks that the checkpoint was written and that the evaluation step prints an accuracy above chance.
